findings.detail: Every one of 24 before/after workspace observations across both OSs finds one visible same-window NSToolbarView with role AXToolbar and zero direct children after modern, advertised public legacy, and navigation-child access. No controls are selected and no native contrast measurements are produced.

Customization26 observes five real NSPopUpButton descendants with effectiveStyle dark and effectiveAppearance DarkAqua while application/window/content are light/Aqua. Equilibrado and Restaurar have alpha1, hidden false and in-window native bounds. Their corresponding original PNG rectangles contain only RGB255. The three other popup bounds are offscreen; their appearance mismatch is recorded but their visual result is not inferred.

The new SDK26 customization PNG is byte-identical to focal2f (SHA256 a8cc670cd1a3dc7ad6d783a8634d30caf4348e1b680600d9d4392445a4683fe2). The controls remain visibly absent. The reentry-owner change did not resolve this captured defect.
Customization on27 records no native NSPopUpButton providers, while the two controls are visible in the original image. The empty native list is not a missing-control failure.

limitations: The two customization originals were opened at original resolution for this technical diagnosis. The full 14-image visual review belongs to scope_audit in /tmp/pdf-appearance-877-independent-review.{md,json}.

Popup bounds and effective appearances were observed immediately after PNG creation; there is no per-popup before-capture snapshot proving stability. Pixel observations report the original corresponding rectangles only.
The runtime fact is empty AX direct children. These originals do not prove that AX client materialization is necessary or sufficient, nor that it would preserve the common rendering state.
The mismatch is a concrete observation, not proof of which SwiftUI/AppKit ancestor or assignment created it. No code or original evidence was changed for this diagnosis.
